channel.title: NearEats Blog
channel.description: Practical advice on finding somewhere good to eat — city guides, eating out with dietary needs, and travel — from the team behind NearEats.

item.title: Why review scores are a bad way to choose a restaurant when travelling
item.description: A 4.4-star place can be unremarkable at home and exceptional abroad. How review scores mislead when you don't know the baseline, and what to check instead.

item.title: Where to eat late in an unfamiliar city: the method that works
item.description: Why kitchens close before doors do, the venue types that genuinely stay open late, and the ten-minute check that saves the walk.

item.title: Wheelchair access in restaurants: the questions that settle the visit
item.description: A restaurant can fail a wheelchair user in two places — the threshold and the table. The checks that settle both before you set off.

item.title: Kosher food away from home: planning without a community to ask
item.description: How to find and verify kosher food while travelling — what the supervision symbols cover, the questions to ask first, and the honest limits.

item.title: Moving to a new city: finding your regular spots in the first month
item.description: How to go from eating by accident to having real regular places — the search radius, the venue types to rotate, and the checklist that settles a table.

item.title: How to find a place open late in a city you don't know
item.description: Why the good places close first, what 22:00 on a menu means, and the working method for finding a place that will actually still be serving at 23:15.

item.title: How to find halal food while travelling, without relying on guesswork
item.description: How to find reliably halal food in a city you don't know: what the label covers, the dishes that are safe by construction, and how to ask first.

item.title: How to find a decent coffee in a city full of chains
item.description: What actually separates a good coffee shop from a chain, what to look for at the counter, and where the independents tend to hide in a city you don't know.

item.title: Eating out with a severe food allergy abroad: what to check
item.description: Eating out with a severe allergy in a city you don't know — the questions that settle a kitchen, the words to write down, and where checking stops helping.

item.title: Eating gluten-free abroad: what to check before you sit down
item.description: A working method for eating gluten-free in a city you don't know — the labels to read, the dishes to be careful about, and the questions that save the evening.

item.title: Food allergies abroad: the phrases and checks that actually work
item.description: How to get a foreign kitchen to take an allergen seriously — the three-line card, the questions that settle it, and the honest limit.
